# Reviewed Pine engine sources

EdgeLab pins PineTS 0.11.0 under AGPL-3.0-only. The original npm package stays unchanged. `scripts/pine-engine.mjs` reconstructs its exact readable sources from the packaged browser source map and applies the reviewed files in `overrides/`. The missing, type-only Indicator barrel comes from the pinned package's declaration re-exports.

`manifest.json` seals the installed version, source-map bytes, declaration barrel, original source bytes and each modified file with SHA-256. Development and production workers use the same source resolver. A changed dependency or patch fails the build until its source and hashes are reviewed together. Imports resolve only to the verified sources and three bundled MIT dependencies; there is no network fetch or arbitrary disk fallback.

The local changes preserve `varip` declarations and object-field metadata, and provide an explicit indicator-only realtime lifecycle for deterministic engine tests. Compiler-generated type metadata retains the upstream type registry and correct method receiver name, including overloaded methods. Ordinary mutable values roll back between updates; intrabar-persistent values and fields retain their appropriate state. Provisional outputs replace the current bar. `setRealtimeMode(true)` is required before `run`; `updateTail(context, { confirmed: false })` recalculates an open bar and `{ confirmed: true }` closes it. Provider bars must remain chronological. Streaming, paginated realtime and strategy tick scheduling are unsupported and fail explicitly.

The primary Binance Live chart uses this lifecycle through a persistent isolated worker per visible native indicator. Other feeds, editor runs and Replay use closed snapshots. `{ received: true }` explicitly executes an accepted provider event even when its OHLCV is unchanged; omitting that flag preserves the engine's unchanged-update shortcut. This integration does not establish TradingView parity. Tests cover supported scalar, collection and declared UDT field rollback, moving-average state and provisional output replacement. Full drawing-object behavior and per-tick performance budgets are not established. Member and type-factory UDT copies use current declared fields, preserve absent/undefined values, and retain shallow references to collections and other objects. See `backend/tests/pine-object-copy55.test.js` for copying tests, `pine-realtime54.test.js` for actual minified-engine lifecycle tests and `pine-engine-integrity54.test.js` for build integrity tests.

Historical object-field receivers are lowered as values in plotting arguments and function returns. Pine v6 uses `(object[offset]).field`; direct field history on registered UDT receivers is rejected with a corrective diagnostic. Pine v5 and JavaScript inputs retain their existing compatibility paths. `backend/tests/pine-object-history56.test.js` verifies existing historical receivers, custom offsets, copied and nested objects, reference identity, typed methods and explicit realtime lifecycle updates. First-bar field access through an absent object is not established by these tests.

Explicit realtime sessions can initialize an entirely closed dataset with `setRealtimeMode(true, { initialTail: "historical" })`. Those bars execute once as confirmed history; the next explicit appended bar starts realtime execution. The default `initialTail: "open"` retains the provisional final-bar behavior.

Realtime rollback state has hard limits of 16,384 mutable nodes, 262,144 mutable cells and 1,280,000 Series slots. Trusted callers may select smaller positive integer limits through `limits: { nodes, cells, seriesSlots }`. Exceeding a limit raises `REALTIME_STATE_LIMIT` and halts that session. Discarded newborn rollback records are released after restoration while historical references, aliases and surviving intrabar state remain available. These are snapshot-state limits, not a total heap or execution-time guarantee: scripts and the underlying engine can allocate memory before snapshot checks. `backend/tests/pine-realtime57.test.js` covers retention, limits and closed-history initialization. `pine-live58.test.js` exercises the genuine minified worker's persistent command protocol, received events, explicit closes, fresh packed buffers and session failures.

Field-level intrabar persistence follows the [Pine objects documentation](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/language/objects/): a persistent object reference does not exempt its ordinary fields from rollback. Excluding discarded newborn field qualifiers from persistence discovery is a local retention policy; TradingView equivalence for discarded-object aliases is not established.

Historical strategy fill recalculation accepts strict boolean `calc_on_order_fills` declarations, including resolved constant and input aliases. The local broker visits open, the nearer extreme, the farther extreme and close in order, executes eligible fills, and awaits the script after each actual fill. Historical callbacks see the final bar OHLCV; newly created orders only use the remaining price path. It preserves one history/output slot per candle, rolls back ordinary script state between executions, and retains the broker ledger and supported `varip` state. The [TradingView execution model](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/language/execution-model/) and [strategy documentation](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/concepts/strategies/#calc_on_order_fills) define the historical fill contract; these tests do not establish complete TradingView equivalence or actual tick-history accuracy.

`backend/tests/pine-strategy65.test.js` checks the actual minified worker's four-fill reversal ledger, brackets created after entries, remaining-path execution, rollback/history, multi-lot partial exits, cancellation/replacement, close timing, fees and slippage. Fill recalculation refuses intrabar margin liquidation with `UNSUPPORTED_ORDER_FILL_CONTEXT`; historical-tick recalculation remains unavailable. Loaded historical bar magnification is described below. Each candle has hard limits of 512 script calculations and 2,048 broker transitions (`STRATEGY_EXECUTION_LIMIT`). Historical rollback uses the existing bounded snapshot graph; the limits do not cover total heap allocation. Live strategies retain their explicit refusal. Omitted/false fill settings retain the original single-calculation broker path.

Explicit `qty_percent=100` unscoped exits use the complete available quantity and persist for subsequent entries until flat. They preserve reservations and normal cancellation/replacement behavior; scoped exits do not attach to entries created after the exit call’s bar and a positive fixed `qty` still takes precedence. Partial percentages and fixed quantities are allocated independently per physical entry when fill recalculation is enabled. The reviewed `cancel_all.ts` override follows the [TradingView cancellation contract](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/concepts/strategies/#strategycancel-and-strategycancel_all): it removes all unfilled entry and exit orders, including pending market closes, without closing filled positions. The minified-worker matrix in `backend/tests/pine-strategy68.test.js` and production sandbox gate `e2e/pine-strategy68.config.ts` cover these behaviors, including the retained single-calculation path.

Historical trailing exits support absolute or entry-relative activation and offsets in instrument ticks. Activation changes broker state without running Pine; an actual fill triggers the configured recalculation. Each physical entry lot retains its own favorable peak, updated only at prices visited after the order exists. Pending replacements preserve that lot's armed state; cancellation, removal of the trailing component and a fresh position retire it. Pine v6 selects the activation reached first when both levels are supplied, while v5 prioritizes the absolute level. Optional `na` arguments are absent; an all-`na` exit disables its previous generation and creates no market close. Malformed distances fail explicitly. Ordinary closed-bar strategies also fill an already armed opening-gap stop at the open before later price-path targets. Incomplete trailing components alongside a valid fixed exit use the fixed exit as a qualified local policy. These are tested historical OHLC semantics, not proof of every TradingView replacement/tie case or live scheduling. See `backend/tests/pine-strategy66.test.js` and `e2e/pine-strategy66.config.ts`.

Modified files retain the original LuxAlgo copyright and AGPL notices, with an EdgeLab modification notice. Matching source distributions must include these overrides, manifest, build script and the locked dependency sources. See the repository licence and third-party notices.

With historical `calc_on_order_fills=true`, fixed or partial-percentage exit generations retain per-entry reservations across later fills. An exhausted generation cannot consume the same lot's remainder automatically; an unscoped generation can cover later lots until flat. Scoped exits retain matching pending entries created before or on the call's bar, even when they fill later. Percentages use each original entry size, and a positive fixed quantity takes precedence. Cancellation/replacement releases the previous generation's reservations. Quantity tolerances follow the supplied increment, so valid `1e-10` quantities and partial remainders are not treated as flat. The shared independent ledgers in `backend/tests/fixtures/pine-strategy70.mjs` run through the actual minified worker and `e2e/pine-strategy70.config.ts` production sandbox gate. This implements the separate-entry model described by [TradingView's strategies documentation](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/concepts/strategies/#exits-for-multiple-entries); fixed-quantity multi-entry sizing is inferred from that model rather than a recorded TradingView comparison. The original single-calculation broker path remains separate, and broader parity is unproven. FIFO closed-trade accounting can differ from the physical lot that supplied an exit price. Live strategy scheduling and intrabar liquidation with fill recalculation or magnification remain unavailable.

Input activation metadata preserves earlier input references and constant aliases as bounded expression data. The host resolves it against validated current values for Check/run and settings controls, without running Pine source on the UI thread. Reviewed overrides are `inputs/analyzeInputs.ts` and `Indicator/scanInputs.ts`; unsupported expressions fail explicitly. The expression protocol permits literals, input references, unary arithmetic/not, logical/comparison/arithmetic operators and ternaries, with at most 64 nodes and depth 7.

Enum input analysis resolves constant aliases through lexical scope, with cycle/persistence/reassignment guards and a maximum alias chain of 256. Each declared member is an immutable, nonplain token interned within its full execution context; field titles are separate display data. The worker bridge uses versioned exact member IDs with declared labels and bounded member lists. Duplicate titles retain distinct comparison, history, array and map-key identity. `str.tostring()` explicitly returns the title, while direct enum arguments to `str.format()` are rejected. The original Pine AST checks enum declarations, assignments, equality comparisons, supported functions/methods, switch branches and collection operations before lowering, including unreachable branches and compatible overloaded calls. This pass rejects recursive functions and bounds inference to 100,000 expression visits and 64 nested calls. These checks do not establish full qualifier inference, all built-in signatures or UDT field typing. Enum method dispatch matches receiver and declared enum argument identities, preserving untyped argument positions. An unresolved `na` or missing argument that matches multiple enum overloads raises an explicit ambiguity error. A variable with a declared enum type retains that type for method selection even when its current value is `na`. Ordinary overloads now emit separate function bindings and select supported exact enum, primitive, collection and declared UDT signatures before execution; integer-to-float promotion is considered after exact matches. Named/default arguments retain their selected parameter order. Generic wrappers specialize for known argument types, retain shared input declaration IDs and preserve separate written-call state; selected nested return calls retain parameter history. Duplicate required signatures and ambiguous or unresolved calls fail explicitly. Full qualified-type inference remains outside this coverage. Supported method calls select their declared receiver and argument signature before lowering; full qualified-type inference remains unverified. The existing unsupported nested-binary historical UDT field path remains separate. See `pine-enum-runtime93.test.js`, `pine-enum-types93.test.js` and `pine-enum-protocol93.test.js` for actual minified-engine and bridge coverage.

`pine-function-overloads94.test.js` runs distinct function bodies, nested history, saved input overrides and strategy quantities through the minified engine. The rules follow [TradingView’s function overload documentation](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/language/user-defined-functions/#function-overloading); this does not establish complete TradingView equivalence.

Native Pine v5 declared UDT variables and typed parameters may shadow built-in namespaces. Lexical field/method receivers, aliases, local scopes and array iteration retain their object values; real namespace calls elsewhere still resolve to built-ins. A UDT method on an object named `input` does not declare an input control. Pine v6 rejects these UDT variable names during preparation, including unused declarations and typed parameters, while ordinary primitive variables and UDT type names retain their existing behavior. The version distinction follows [v5 object shadowing](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/v5/language/objects/#shadowing) and [v6 variable shadowing](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/language/variable-declarations/#shadowing). `pine-namespace-shadowing96.test.js` exercises the genuine minified engine and worker; the namespace cases in `e2e/pine-editor.interaction.spec.ts` check custom inputs, saved-source reload and chart application on desktop and mobile. These tests do not establish every namespace signature, container iteration type or complete TradingView equivalence.

User-defined method overloads retain separate bodies and written-call state. Supported known signatures select exact receiver/argument types before integer-to-float promotion, using the selected declaration’s named/default parameter order. Method-only plain calls retain their explicit receiver; ordinary functions with the same name retain their separate path. Eligible custom collection method signatures coexist with built-in calls. Duplicate required signatures, ambiguous `na` and unresolved argument types fail explicitly rather than selecting an arbitrary body. The rules follow [TradingView’s method overloading documentation](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/language/methods/#method-overloading). `pine-method-overloads97.test.js` exercises the genuine minified engine and worker, and the method cases in `e2e/pine-editor.interaction.spec.ts` cover editor inputs, saved reload and chart application. This coverage does not establish all qualified types, built-in signatures or complete TradingView equivalence.

Pine v5/v6 primitive variables and parameters named after a namespace can call supported custom-only methods through their lexical value. Existing public namespace members retain native precedence, including when a custom receiver signature could otherwise match. Selected method receivers retain overload argument ordering, written-call history and persistent locals; custom calls on a variable named `input` do not create controls. The source-sealed `namespace-members.json` records public members of the reviewed initialized engine, excluding private helpers. `rtk proxy node scripts/pine-namespace-members101.mjs --check` regenerates and compares this inventory; after a reviewed namespace-source update, regenerate it and review its manifest hash. The generated compiler lookup is supplied only by the verified source resolver. `pine-primitive-shadowing101.test.js` covers the actual minified engine and worker. The combination follows TradingView’s primitive [variable shadowing](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/language/variable-declarations/#shadowing) and [custom methods](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/language/methods/#method-overloading) rules; this inventory is the pinned engine’s API, and complete TradingView parity remains unproven.

The reviewed member inventory adds approximately 9 KB to the deferred Pine compiler worker. The worker ceilings are 818,000 raw bytes and 218,500 gzip bytes after adding actual higher-timeframe execution, request dependency metadata and bounded Pine v5 static wrapper extraction owned intrabar execution and historical bar magnification and bounded line-drawing transport/rollback. The magnifier build measured 812,718 raw bytes (2,896 bytes above the preceding build); The line-drawing worker measured 816,474 raw / 217,496 gzip bytes; only this deferred worker ceiling changed. Public, authenticated and chart loading budgets remain unchanged. Run `rtk npm run check:ui-performance` after building to check the actual asset sizes and dependency graphs.

Both native `request.security` and `request.security_lower_tf` validate the original exchange-qualified symbol and timeframe before any same-timeframe or secondary-context shortcut. The worker owns an immutable provider callback captured when each request namespace is constructed. Empty chart aliases and whole-symbol case matches resolve to the supplied chart identity; bare ticker aliases on exchange-qualified charts, different exchanges, unsupported timeframes, encoded session/adjustment modifiers and nonstandard candle requests fail with `UNAVAILABLE_DATA`. Failure prevents snapshot/strategy publication and halts a persistent live session. Renko, Kagi, Line Break and Point & Figure ticker builders retain a distinct encoded chart-type identity instead of silently returning a standard ticker; they do not generate those candles or claim TradingView ticker-string equivalence. Explicit `ticker.standard` removes modifiers and can request the matching standard chart. `backend/tests/pine-request-identity103.test.js` exercises the actual minified worker in Pine v5/v6, saved inputs, named/nested/custom-method calls, live rollback and strategy quantities. Additional-symbol, calendar/session and transformed-candle execution remain unavailable. Historical lower-timeframe execution requires the explicit owned source snapshot described below; persistent live lower-timeframe execution remains unavailable.

Historical `request.security` supports complete same-symbol UTC intraday multiples of the loaded chart timeframe. Each target bucket requires every consecutive source candle on its UTC grid; partial or missing groups are omitted with a visible data warning, and insufficient history returns `na`. The engine evaluates the isolated original expression on target OHLCV with native saved input IDs, full ticker identity and closed bar states. Historical lookahead off publishes at target close; on publishes at open, including its usual future-looking behavior. `gaps_on` emits only availability boundaries, while `gaps_off` carries the last available value through omitted or trailing buckets. `calc_bars_count` limits available remote history and warmup. Pine v6 indicators default to dynamic requests; explicit dynamic requests can reevaluate supported nested contexts. Static nested dependencies (`dynamic_requests=false`, including the v5 default) retain the original chart calculation: an isolated compiler slice captures each actual request return on the original chart, samples it at target close, and evaluates outer operations on target history. Outer lookahead controls publication afterward. Scalar and tuple histories preserve missing values, source and saved input IDs; known top-level functions select the isolated slice for their full compiled call chain, including nested wrappers, and fully named expressions retain native parameter identities; incomplete captures, unsupported lexical or dynamic function references, unsafe shared-state dependencies and collection/object transport fail explicitly. Supported Pine v5 conditional wrapped static requests extract only requested calculations; wrapper state and side effects retain their original activation. This historical sampling model is checked against independent numerical examples and the documented static-context rule, not a direct TradingView execution comparison. Named argument bags use sealed expression binding analysis. Unsupported expression shapes fail rather than running an unbound whole script.

Historical intrabar requests can use an optional `sourceSnapshot: { timeframe, bars }` of actual loaded candles for the chart symbol. Source history has at most 200,000 candles, chart history at most 20,000; validation copies ordinary OHLCV fields and requires ordered unique UTC-epoch-aligned fixed intraday timeframes, source duration dividing the chart duration, and source candles within the supplied chart window. Callers also clip source candles to the actual replay cursor; the worker never fetches data or fabricates missing candles. Same-timeframe chart candles remain authoritative even if a source snapshot is supplied. The actual supplied source timeframe is available directly, including non-day-divisor durations. Other requested lower timeframes require fixed UTC-day-aligned multiples of the source duration up to the current chart/context duration; derived non-day-divisor and calendar durations remain unavailable. All non-chart derived candles, including higher-timeframe requests, require complete consecutive actual source groups; a partial displayed chart tail cannot prove a complete larger candle. Each actual complete child's opening timestamp assigns it to a chart bar; thus a globally available complete 2-minute candle opening at minute 4 belongs to the 0–5-minute chart bar, while an incomplete derived candle at the current replay boundary is absent. This opening-membership rule follows the pinned engine; exact cross-boundary TradingView parity has not been independently established. Historical `request.security` selects the first available child with lookahead on and the last with lookahead off; missing chart intervals return `na` with gaps on or carry the previous available value with gaps off. `request.security_lower_tf` returns chronological arrays, or a tuple of arrays, including empty arrays for absent intrabar history. Its owned path evaluates the isolated original expression with native input IDs, full written call-chain identity and the existing request-depth guards, without a whole-script fallback or singleton secondary shortcut. Static nested primitive intrabar arrays are copied and reconstructed rather than retaining mutable aliases; ordinary requested object/collection sampling remains outside the supported transport. Request parameter histories snapshot time and scalar helpers at each executing bar, including UDF-returned tuples. Secondary prefix slices omit proven dead intrabar requests and read-only consumers instead of rebinding their chart-only array reads to a child timeframe. Unrelated mutation-bearing or unknown consumer prerequisites cannot yet be projected safely and fail with a compile-time isolation diagnostic. Prefix projection is bounded to 65,536 traversal steps and 128 nesting levels per slice. Unsupported isolation shapes fail explicitly. Supplied source snapshots are historical-only: streaming secondary updates have not been implemented.

Secondary execution retains the chart loop limit, at most 64 provider snapshots and eight nested contexts. Cumulative requested candle slots and retained secondary Series histories (including function scopes), returned intrabar-array payloads and static captured/decoded values each stop at 1,280,000. Series accounting occurs after calculation and does not bound peak allocation or collection payloads; worker deadlines and isolation still apply. Persistent live higher-timeframe execution and exchange-aligned calendar/session data remain unavailable. Static original-chart replays share the same context, snapshot and history limits; repeated captures of one bar replace its value with accounting adjusted by retained tuple nodes, and sparse captures cannot pass completeness checks. `pine-higher-timeframe104.test.js` and `pine-static-requests105.test.js` use independent aggregation/merge/strategy oracles against the actual minified worker; the production browser check is in `e2e/pine-runtime.interaction.spec.ts`. These gates establish the described cases, not complete TradingView equivalence.

Request isolation follows known declaration calls through up to eight written function levels. The compiler bounds generated slices to 256 per script and reverse call-path traversal to 4,096 edges per requested expression. Function identities remain active across awaited requests and are released on settlement, keeping later nested local state separate for each written root path. Static replay does not publish replay orders or plots. Referenced mutable global state, reassigned globals and unresolved reference results that cannot be reproduced by an isolated expression are rejected before replay; this prevents an apparently valid but incorrect substituted history. Collection namespace results stored in referenced globals are classified conservatively, so even scalar collection queries can be refused until their return shape is established. Independently scoped function-local histories remain supported in the verified examples. `pine-nested-functions106.test.js` checks nested arguments, named expressions, tuples, history, native input IDs, asynchronous call identity, strategy quantities, symbol authority and request limits through the actual sealed minified worker.

Pine v5 static non-exported request wrappers called conditionally or from loops use bounded compiler extraction: each written call receives globally evaluated request results while its original body and unused arguments remain conditional. Immutable wrapper-local declaration dependencies are evaluated once in a separate requested calculation; unrelated before/after state is retained in the wrapper. Known nested wrappers retain separate written identities through eight levels, with at most 256 generated functions, 4,096 fresh identifiers and 100,000 shared compiler traversal/copy/resolution operations. Loop-dependent arguments, mutable, tuple-dependent or lexically shadowed local expression dependencies and unproved simple symbol/timeframe dependencies fail explicitly as unsupported isolation shapes. Pine v6 static wrapped calls in conditional operands or local blocks are rejected, including unreachable branches; dynamic calls retain their existing behavior. Direct static requests nested inside a conditional/loop within a function are conservatively rejected by this supported-subset policy; the verified documentation does not separately establish that inner-function shape. This supported subset does not establish complete request qualifier checking or TradingView translation equivalence. See [TradingView’s local-scope request rules](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/concepts/other-timeframes-and-data/#in-local-scopes) and [the v5 translation example](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/v5/writing/profiling-and-optimization/).

In the verified PineTS conditional-wrapper cases, dynamic requested calculations retain sparse activation history; static extraction evaluates the requested expression on every available target candle. The independent numerical tests distinguish these cases. Exact conditional TradingView behavior has not been independently calibrated.

Historical bar magnification accepts resolved boolean `use_bar_magnifier` declarations and explicit saved test settings, alongside `calc_on_order_fills`. It uses the actual supplied smaller-timeframe snapshot for complete consecutive groups whose aggregate OHLC matches the chart candle. Source candles are bounded to 200,000 and use the existing fixed UTC intraday grid; missing or incomplete groups use the chart OHLC path, with `BAR_MAGNIFIER_COVERAGE` reporting covered and fallback candles. Complete price mismatches fail with `UNAVAILABLE_DATA`. Each smaller candle follows the broker’s assumed open → nearer extreme → farther extreme → close path; gaps between children fill at the next child open, without inventing intermediate prices. Fill timestamps use the actual source candle opening time, not an observed tick time; trade indexes, calculations, inputs, chart OHLCV, TA and history remain chart-based. Magnification alone calculates once at chart close; fill recalculation adds executions after actual fills and keeps the existing rollback and `varip` rules. Orders cannot revisit earlier child prices, including on the initial declaration bar. Paths traverse at most 200,000 children without allocating a flattened price array, while each chart candle separately permits 512 calculations and 2,048 broker events. Intrabar margin liquidation and historical-tick/live strategy scheduling still fail explicitly. The minified-worker oracles are in `backend/tests/pine-bar-magnifier115.test.js`; production sandbox and actual editor checks use the corresponding `e2e/pine-magnifier115.config.ts` and `e2e/pine-magnifier-editor115.config.ts` gates. These establish the described loaded-data cases, not full TradingView equivalence, exchange/session alignment or actual tick replay. See [TradingView’s historical-detail documentation](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/concepts/strategies/#adjusting-historical-bar-detail).

The line-drawing patch adds known `LineObject` scalar payload fields and each `LineHelper` active list to the existing bounded realtime rollback graph. It retains the original backing-array identity before each forming candle and restores it before payload restoration, because native synchronization replaces/compacts that list. This restores setters, deletion and oldest-line eviction while retaining object IDs and methods; helper/context closures are never traversed. Output transport and chart rendering remain separate from engine calculations. The manifest records the reviewed source hash; installed npm sources are unchanged. The line gate exercises both Pine versions, final object snapshots, provisional rollback, and real production-worker/chart rendering; it does not establish full TradingView equivalence.

Native `linefill.new`, getters, color updates and deletion render final active fills between line drawings, with at most 500 transported fills outside numeric plot/channel buffers. Boundary strokes can be `na` or transparent independently of fill color. Replacing the same unordered line pair creates a new fill ID; stale handles cannot change the replacement. Line deletion and native line eviction delete linked fills. Realtime rollback restores committed fill IDs, membership, colors and referenced lines after provisional replacement/deletion/eviction. Rendering clips crossing lobes to the pane and reads current transforms after pan, resize, log or inverted scale changes. Fills retain an established scale; an otherwise empty study pane can seed its range from visible boundaries. Overlay fills cannot expand the primary price scale. The shared horizontal domain, unequal/reversed endpoints and vertical zero-area geometry use disclosed local policies; exact TradingView geometry is unverified. Cross-pane boundaries are omitted with a visible warning. Polylines and tables remain unavailable. After building, `rtk proxy npx playwright test --config=e2e/pine-linefills122.config.ts` and `rtk proxy npx playwright test --config=e2e/pine-linefills-editor122.config.ts` check genuine production-worker chart and editor behavior; independent engine/protocol/geometry checks are in `backend/tests/pine-linefills122.test.js`. The worker raw-size budget increases by 2,000 bytes for bounded line-fill transport and lifecycle handling; page and compressed-worker budgets remain unchanged.

Native Pine boxes now preserve final active `box.new`, setters, getters, copies and deletion in one drawing host per placement, separately bounded to 500 objects outside numeric plot channels. Both coordinate and chart-point constructors retain declared `xloc` (bar index by default), including missing point coordinates; time values remain milliseconds inside the engine and seconds in transport. Numeric text sizes and constructor `text_formatting` are retained. Persistent method copies initialize once, including boxed fields and function-returned receivers; ordinary copies continue on each bar. Live rollback restores existing box coordinates, colors, borders, text, deletion and FIFO membership, including objects whose creation return was discarded, without traversing helper closures.

Borders, background and text colors are independent. Solid, dashed and dotted borders use widths 0–16; zero-width/height rectangles retain their remaining border, while identical corners or missing coordinates paint nothing. Extended horizontal borders retain authored vertical sides; the background and text use the finite authored rectangle, an explicitly local policy where extended-background parity is unverified. Reversed corners are normalized. Visible boxes and overflowing unwrapped text can contribute their numeric bounds to autoscale; completely invisible boxes do not. Native box order paints each fill/border/text together above line drawings. Text remains plain canvas text, with no HTML or URL evaluation. Text sizes are bounded to 0–512 and strings to 4096 characters; `size.auto` uses a stable 14-pixel local default. String sizes map tiny/small/normal/large/huge to 8/10/14/20/36. Alignment uses authored coordinates even after clipping; explicit newlines are preserved. Unwrapped text may overflow box borders and is clipped by the pane. Automatic wrapping measures words/characters within the box and clips to its rectangle. Default/system and monospace fonts, bold/italic and their combination are supported. Font metrics, padding, wrapping, dash phase and exact TradingView pixels remain uncalibrated. Unsupported settings produce visible omissions. Polylines and tables remain unavailable.

After building, `rtk proxy npx playwright test --config=e2e/pine-boxes123.config.ts` exercises genuine production-worker/chart geometry, text, scales, clipping and live updates; `rtk proxy npx playwright test --config=e2e/pine-boxes-editor123.config.ts` exercises saved custom-input reruns and fill/text cleanup in the real editor. Independent sealed engine, protocol and recorded geometry tests are in `backend/tests/pine-boxes123.test.js`. The reviewed worker budget increases by 6,000 raw and 2,000 compressed bytes for bounded box metadata, constructor fixes and rollback payloads; page budgets remain unchanged.

Native Pine labels now render final active objects, including getters/setters, copies, deletion and FIFO limits, with at most 500 plain label payloads outside numeric plot channels. Both coordinate and chart-point constructors default to bar indexes; millisecond time coordinates convert to seconds only in transport. Positional/named NA text clears glyphs while retaining the shape. Colors are independently nullable; omitted native color/textcolor use local blue/white defaults. Native text sizes use label-specific 7/10/12/18/24 mappings; numeric sizes 0–512, explicit newlines, alignment, default/monospace fonts and bold/italic formatting are supported. Auto uses a stable local 12px default. All 21 pinned label styles, including plain and outlined text, use disclosed local canvas geometry; exact TradingView pixels and session extrapolation remain unverified.

Price labels follow actual price/log/inverted transforms, including future chart whitespace. Above/below labels ignore y (including NA) and anchor above/below the actual referenced candle; missing or future candles are not fabricated. Normal labels render above boxes within their chart layer; forced labels render over the main chart even for a behind-chart overlay script. Labels share the owned drawing host per placement. Visible ink can seed the numeric range; physical padding is correctly mapped on inverted scales and capped jointly to 20% of pane height and available drawable height. Oversized glyphs retain their original sizes and clip to the pane. Cached glyph metrics bound redraws to visible rows. Hover tooltips use safe plain text, actual label hit geometry, theme colors and an owned chart-relative container; pan, price-transform/size changes and disposal retire stale tooltips.

Live rollback restores existing label fields and backing-array membership after provisional setters, copies, deletion or collection, including discarded-return objects. Persistent copies initialize once; ordinary copies retain per-bar behavior. After building, run `rtk proxy npx playwright test --config=e2e/pine-labels124.config.ts` and `rtk proxy npx playwright test --config=e2e/pine-labels-editor124.config.ts` for genuine production-worker chart/editor/live checks; independent engine/protocol tests are in `backend/tests/pine-labels124.test.js`. The worker raw budget increases by 5,000 bytes for label transport and rollback; compressed-worker and page budgets stay unchanged. This verifies the covered local cases, not complete TradingView equivalence.

Native lines, boxes and labels retain independent `force_overlay` flags through the strict worker bridge. Ordinary drawings follow the indicator's behind-chart setting; forced drawings always use the main chart's front layer. Each placement keeps one owned drawing host and all active boundary references; fill, line, box and label z-order is retained independently within each layer. Copies and live rollback keep their original flags. Strict line/box payloads now have 12/21 fields and require placement to equal the script overlay setting or the object's force flag. Line fills derive the pinned engine's force flag from either active boundary; mixed forced/ordinary boundary layering is a disclosed local policy, with TradingView calibration unverified. Native engine sources and dependencies are unchanged. Genuine engine/protocol tests and production-worker chart pixels are covered by `backend/tests/pine-force-overlay125.test.js` and `e2e/pine-force-overlay125.config.ts`.

Native Pine polylines now render final active point snapshots, straight or uniform Catmull–Rom cubic segments, open/closed paths, independent NA stroke/fill colors, all six line styles and forced main-chart front placement. Creation owns copies of chart-point coordinates; delete/all/FIFO collection and live provisional deletion/GC restore payloads and the original helper list. Polylines have no invented copy/getter/setter API. The strict bridge uses 11 fields and `{x,y}` point pairs, at most 100 drawings/10,000 points each/32,000 cumulative points, and the existing cumulative 1 MB metadata/structural and realtime graph limits. Unrepresentable curve controls omit the affected run without creating replacement edges or scale contributions. NA points split open strokes and suppress fills/closed seams; fills implicitly close open paths and use nonzero winding. Curves use local screen-space uniform Catmull–Rom interpolation with possible overshoot; visible cubic extrema participate in autoscale, including reversed and looping x coordinates. The local polyline layer sits above boxes and below labels. Spline metrics, NA policy, winding, arrow geometry and layer placement have not been calibrated against TradingView. Timestamp gaps keep the existing chart-owned interpolation policy without fabricated candles. Upstream AGPL notices and matching-source checks remain intact. Native/protocol tests and actual production-worker chart coverage live in `backend/tests/pine-polylines126.test.js` and `e2e/pine-polylines126.config.ts`.

Polyline transport and point ownership add about 5.3 kB raw/1.2 kB gzip to the native worker versus iteration 125. Its isolated budget is now 836,000 raw/222,000 gzip bytes; route, workspace and other asset budgets stay unchanged.
